basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Qui cum vidisset, surrexit, et ivit obviam eis; adoravitque pronus in terra, et dixit:'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Qui cum vidisset, surrexit, et ivit obviam eis; adoravitque pronus in terra, et dixit: Obsecro, Domine, declinate in domum pueri vestri, et manete ibi, et caetera. Magnum perfectumque in beato Lot exemplum Deo devotae hospitalitatis ostenditur, qui ingredientes urbem hospites non solum occurrens excipere paratus fuit, verum etiam ut ad se diverterent secumque requiescerent obnixius postulabat. Renuebant autem primo domum ejus intrare, quod tamen postmodum eo compellente facere consenserunt, ut sic industriam hospitalitatis ejus diligentius probarent; probatam dignius remunerarent, dum eum a peccantium interitu cum sua domo eriperent.
